articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs reported that 16 Indian nationals, including 10 seamen, have been killed in the ongoing West Asia conflict. Another 75 Indians have been injured. The government stated it is coordinating with local authorities for the early repatriation of mortal remains and providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families during the crisis.

articles.headline: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 10; missiles hit Poland
articles.summary: A massive wave of Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine killed at least 10 people and injured over 50. Poland's military reported that a Russian cruise missile briefly entered its airspace before re-entering Ukraine, heightening NATO-Russia tensions. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy renewed his plea for advanced air defense systems to protect civilian infrastructure.

articles.headline: Rushdie attacker Hadi Matar found guilty of terrorism charges
articles.summary: A US federal jury found Hadi Matar guilty of terrorism charges for the 2022 stabbing of author Salman Rushdie. Matar faces a maximum sentence of life imprisonment. The prosecution successfully argued the attack was motivated by a fatwa against Rushdie's book 'The Satanic Verses'. Rushdie, who lost an eye in the attack, was not required to testify during the trial.

articles.headline: Dilip Gavit wins gold in men's T47 100m sprint
articles.summary: Indian para-athlete Dilip Gavit clinched the gold medal in the men's T47 100m event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, clocking 10.71 seconds. In a remarkable double podium finish for India, Mohammed Basil secured the silver medal. Gavit credited his success to his coach who mentored him after a childhood accident led to his impairment.

articles.headline: Assam flood toll rises to 80; 2 lakh people affected
articles.summary: The death toll from the devastating floods in Assam has increased to 80 as heavy rains continue. Over 2 lakh people across multiple districts remain displaced or severely affected. Rescue teams from the NDRF and SDRF are conducting relief operations, while the state government has set up hundreds of relief camps to provide food and medical assistance to those hit by the deluge.

articles.headline: PM Modi urges energy independence amid global supply crisis
articles.summary: Prime Minister Modi has called for accelerated efforts toward national energy independence in response to supply chain disruptions caused by the West Asia conflict. During a review meeting, the PM emphasized increasing domestic production and transitioning to green energy sources. He assured that current fuel stocks are sufficient to meet immediate national demand.

articles.headline: Meta updates security protocols for VIP accounts after controversy
articles.summary: Meta has implemented new security protocols for 'VIP' accounts following a row over the temporary removal of a video from PM Modi's page. The electronics and IT ministry stated that Meta expressed regret and is refining its automated moderation systems. The new measures include human oversight before any actions are taken against accounts of high-ranking global officials.

articles.headline: 12km elevated road proposed to connect Noida and Ghaziabad
articles.summary: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has proposed a new 12km six-lane elevated road to bypass the congested GT Road stretch. The ₹2,000 crore project will link the Delhi-Meerut Expressway with the NH-91 junction, significantly improving travel time for commuters heading toward the upcoming Noida International Airport at Jewar and regional industrial hubs.

articles.headline: Delhi government to digitize rural property and family records
articles.summary: The Delhi government is launching a 'Family Card' initiative for rural residents, integrating property records with family details. The scheme aims to simplify access to welfare programs and resolve land disputes through GIS mapping. The first phase will cover 30 villages, providing residents with a unique digital identity that serves as proof for various government services.

articles.headline: China establishes high-altitude drone R&D center near Everest
articles.summary: China has opened a new research and development center for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in Tibet, located near Mount Everest. The facility will test drones designed for high-altitude logistics, surveillance, and environmental monitoring. The center is part of China's strategy to enhance its technological capabilities and infrastructure in the sensitive Himalayan border region.

articles.headline: X and OpenAI sue Minnesota over 'nunnification' technology law
articles.summary: Tech giants X and OpenAI have filed a lawsuit against the US state of Minnesota, challenging a law that restricts the use of 'nunnification' technology. The law aims to prevent AI-generated deepfakes and explicit content. The companies argue the legislation is overly broad and infringes on free speech rights, potentially hindering legitimate technological development.

articles.headline: Japan quake toll reaches 34 as heatwave hampers rescue
articles.summary: The death toll from the earthquake in Japan's Kumamoto region has risen to 34. Rescue operations are facing extreme difficulties as temperatures soar above 34 degrees Celsius. Thousands of residents remain in emergency shelters without adequate cooling or water supplies. Authorities are working to restore power and communications while warning of potential heat-related illnesses.

articles.headline: Govt reports 417 Indians deported from US in 2025
articles.summary: The government informed Parliament that 417 Indian nationals were deported from the United States in the year 2025. This marked a significant rise compared to previous years. Officials stated that many deportations were linked to illegal immigration and visa violations. The government is working with US authorities to crack down on human trafficking syndicates promoting illegal travel.

articles.headline: Endangered Great Indian Bustard chicks hatch in Rajasthan
articles.summary: In a victory for conservation efforts, eleven Great Indian Bustard (GIB) chicks have hatched at a breeding facility in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. The GIB is a critically endangered species with fewer than 150 birds remaining in the wild. The newly hatched chicks will be reared for eventual release into the desert habitat to help boost the struggling wild population.

articles.headline: Delhi to drop cases against protesters with clean records
articles.summary: The Delhi government has announced it will not take further legal action against individuals involved in recent NEET-UG protests, provided they have no prior criminal history. This relief applies only to peaceful demonstrators; those involved in violence or vandalism will still face prosecution. The decision follows a Supreme Court directive regarding the handling of student protests.

articles.headline: Sonam Wangchuk hails exam reform bill, seeks Ladakh commitments
articles.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk welcomed the passage of the Public Examinations Amendment Bill in Parliament, saying it will protect student interests. However, he urged the Union government to honor written agreements regarding Ladakh's administrative status and environmental protection. Wangchuk emphasized that fulfilling these promises is essential to maintaining trust in the region.

articles.headline: SC: Hospitals likely refused girl treatment due to poverty
articles.summary: The Supreme Court expressed shock that private hospitals in Ghaziabad likely turned away a minor sexual assault victim because of her family's poverty. The girl died after being denied emergency care. The Court has directed a high-level SIT to investigate the medical negligence and ordered the state government to ensure that no patient is ever denied life-saving treatment for financial reasons.

articles.headline: Hyderabad police name Meta India head in PM post cases
articles.summary: Hyderabad's cybercrime unit has registered cases against the head of Meta India and several others for hosting manipulated videos of Prime Minister Modi. The action follows complaints from BJP supporters who alleged the content was intended to mislead the public. Police have sought account details from Meta to identify the creators of the offensive posts and take further legal action.

articles.headline: Pellet survivor Insha Mushtaq receives gas agency funding
articles.summary: Eight years after being blinded by pellet gun fire, Insha Mushtaq has been granted ₹41.2 lakh by the J&K government to establish a gas agency. The funding fulfills a 2018 rehabilitation pledge. Insha, who became a symbol of the 2016 protests, has since completed her graduation using Braille. She thanked the government for the support, which will help her achieve financial independence.

articles.headline: Karnataka man arrested in Kerala after 37 years on run
articles.summary: A 57-year-old man, absconding since 1989 after a robbery in Karnataka, was arrested by Kerala police in Deksha. The accused had been living under a false identity for nearly four decades. A Karnataka police team traced him following a tip-off. He was produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody, bringing an end to one of the state's longest-running manhunts.

articles.headline: 'Dead' woman in Bareilly wakes up before her funeral
articles.summary: In a miraculous event, a 65-year-old woman in Bareilly, declared dead by hospital staff, began breathing just as her family prepared for her last rites. The woman had been under treatment for a liver ailment. Hospital authorities have launched a formal inquiry into the medical team that issued the death certificate, while the patient is now receiving intensive care.

articles.headline: Hockey team's saffron jersey switch sparks intense public debate
articles.summary: The Indian hockey team's decision to wear saffron jerseys for the 2026 Commonwealth Games has met with mixed reactions. Former players criticized the move for abandoning the traditional blue color used since 1928. The hockey federation defended the choice, stating it reflects national pride. Some fans have welcomed the change, while others view it as an unnecessary politicization of sports.

articles.headline: Delhi college life costs up to ₹3 lakh annually
articles.summary: A study on the cost of education in Delhi reveals that students from outside the city spend up to ₹3 lakh per year on living expenses, including rent, food, and transport. This is nearly four times the ₹70,000 spent by local students living with family. High accommodation costs near university campuses are identified as the single largest financial burden for out-of-town students.

articles.headline: Ukraine seeks India's peace role amid maritime attack concerns
articles.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Minister has reached out to India, requesting a more active role in peace negotiations as attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea and West Asia rise. Kyiv emphasized India's global influence as a neutral party that could help stabilize maritime trade routes. India reiterated its commitment to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the ongoing conflict.

articles.headline: Govt Review May Let Telcos Slice Up Net Neutrality
articles.summary: The government is considering a review of 2018 net neutrality rules to allow telecom operators to offer differentiated connectivity and speeds for specialized services like 5G slicing. Telcos argue current norms are too rigid for technological advancements in healthcare and smart factories. Any changes would require guardrails to prevent 'walled gardens' and ensure non-discriminatory access.

articles.headline: Rajya Sabha Passes Exam Bill Amid Opposition Walkout
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill to address paper leaks. The passage occurred as Opposition members, led by Mallikarjun Kharge, staged a walkout. They were protesting the government's refusal to discuss separate issues, including the alleged use of force and pellet guns against student protesters during a recent march in Delhi.

articles.headline: RBI Draws the Line on Retail Term Deposit Pricing
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has issued revised guidelines prohibiting banks from offering differential interest rates on retail term deposits based on whether they are 'callable' or 'non-callable'. The move aims to simplify deposit products for retail customers. Banks must now align pricing more closely with liquidity costs and ensure transparency across different categories of deposits.

articles.headline: Global Workforce Layoffs Reach Indian Units of Tech Giants
articles.summary: Restructuring efforts at global firms like Visa, Walmart, and Amazon are leading to job cuts in their Indian operations. Visa is laying off approximately 2,600 employees globally, including roles in India, as it pivots toward AI-focused positions. Walmart and Amazon are also reducing headcounts in specific local teams to reorganize their global platforms and consolidate operations.

articles.headline: India Inc Steps Up Festive Hiring by 8-25 Percent
articles.summary: Temporary recruitment in India is projected to rise between 8% and 25% this festive season compared to last year. E-commerce, logistics, and retail sectors are driving the surge, with some firms expecting 40-60% growth in seasonal roles. Hiring is expanding significantly into tier-2 and tier-3 cities as companies prepare for high consumer demand despite global economic uncertainties.

articles.headline: Sarvam AI Building End-to-End Stack to Challenge Giants
articles.summary: Indian startup Sarvam is developing an end-to-end software and infrastructure stack to compete with global AI leaders like OpenAI. Having recently raised $234 million, the firm is valued at $1.5 billion. Their strategy focuses on creating cost-effective, localized AI models tailored for Indian languages and enterprise needs, aiming to secure India's position in the global AI race.

articles.headline: US GDP Growth Slows to 1.5% Amid Rising Imports
articles.summary: The US economy expanded at a 1.5% annual rate in the second quarter of 2026, down from 2.1% in the previous quarter. The slowdown was driven by a surge in imports and the impact of sustained high interest rates on consumer spending. Despite the cooling growth, the labor market remains resilient, with moderate job additions helping to avoid a more significant economic downturn.

articles.headline: M&M Net Jumps 34% Despite Higher Input Costs
articles.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra reported a 34% increase in consolidated net profit for the June quarter, reaching ₹3,487 crore. The growth was driven by strong demand for its SUV portfolio and a 28% rise in consolidated revenue. However, the company noted that rising raw material costs and commodity inflation have started to impact margins in its automotive and farm equipment segments.

articles.headline: LS Clears Vande Mataram Bill Amid Opposition Protest
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed a bill making insults to the national song, Vande Mataram, a punishable offense. The legislation was approved via voice vote even as DMK and AIADMK members opposed it, arguing that such mandates could infringe on federalism and secularism. The bill prescribes fines and potential imprisonment for actions that intentionally disrespect the national song.

articles.headline: Maha FDA Targets Overpriced Drugs in Special Drive
articles.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking action against pharmacies and hospitals selling medicines at prices exceeding the Ceiling Price set by the NPPA. Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe stated that the agency has identified overpricing in essential drugs, including cardiac stents. The FDA is also tightening manufacturing standards to ensure compliance with WHO-GMP norms.

articles.headline: Avaada Secures $1.3 Billion Loan for Green Energy Projects
articles.summary: Avaada Group has secured approximately ₹12,800 crore ($1.3 billion) in funding from a consortium of lenders led by SBI, REC, and BoB. The capital will fund 1.35 GW of hybrid renewable energy projects and 800 MW of solar capacity in Gujarat and Maharashtra. The projects are expected to be commissioned by March 2027, supporting India's transition to non-fossil fuel energy sources.

articles.headline: IndiGo Q4 Profit Doubles to ₹1,895 Crore; JSW Steel Net Profit Slumps
articles.summary: InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo) reported a 106% jump in Q4 net profit to ₹1,895 crore, with record annual profit of ₹8,176 crore and plans for a business class. Conversely, JSW Steel’s Q4 net profit fell 64.5% to ₹1,299 crore due to high raw material costs and lower prices, despite stable revenue of ₹46,269 crore. The board recommended a ₹7.30 dividend.

articles.headline: Tata Steel Q1 Net Profit Rises to ₹2,318 Crore; Approves Mega Expansion
articles.summary: Tata Steel reported a consolidated net profit rise to approximately ₹2,318–2,385 crore for Q1 FY27, with revenue at ₹60,794 crore. Despite high input costs, domestic sales grew 2% to 7.27 million tonnes. The board approved a ₹33,873 crore investment in Neelachal Ispat Nigam (Odisha) to expand capacity by 4.8 million tonnes. Quarterly capital expenditure stood at ₹3,579 crore.

articles.headline: Hyundai Motor India Q1 Profit Drops 35% Amid West Asia Supply Disruptions
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor India’s Q1 net profit fell 35% to approximately ₹887–889 crore, while revenue declined 0.5% to ₹16,334.6 crore. Performance was hit by a vendor facility fire and the West Asia/Red Sea crisis impacting exports. While domestic sales grew 5.4%, output constraints weighed on results. The company plans a ₹7,500 crore expenditure in FY25 for new models and plant upgrades.

articles.headline: Mahindra & Mahindra Q1 Profit Surges 34% Driven by Record SUV Demand
articles.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra reported a 34–37% jump in Q1 consolidated net profit to ₹5,455–5,998 crore, with revenue up 28% to ₹58,188 crore. Growth was powered by robust SUV demand (1.75 lakh units) and a 43.1% market share in tractors. The company plans to double manufacturing capacity by FY31 via expansion in Chakan and a new Nagpur plant, targeting 82,000 vehicles monthly by year-end.

articles.headline: Maruti Suzuki Gujarat Plant Becomes Suzuki's Largest Global Site at 10 Lakh Units
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki has commenced commercial production at its fourth unit in Hansalpur, Gujarat, following a ₹3,900 crore investment. This adds 2.5 lakh units, bringing the facility’s total capacity to 10 lakh units—Suzuki’s largest globally. The site will manufacture the flagship eVX electric vehicles. Maruti’s total Indian manufacturing capacity now reaches 29 lakh units annually.

articles.headline: SEBI Launches Green Channel Mechanism for Faster Alternative Investment Fund Approvals
articles.summary: Market regulator SEBI has introduced an operational framework for a 'Green-Channel' mechanism to accelerate Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) launches. The system allows certain funds to launch schemes immediately after filing a placement memorandum. Schemes failing to comply with the revised GARUDA mechanism will face extra monitoring. The move aims to improve the ease of doing business.

articles.headline: Bajaj Finance Q1 Profit Grows 29% as Assets Under Management Surge
articles.summary: Bajaj Finance reported a 29% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to ₹4,765 crore for Q1 FY27, with standalone profit at ₹5,346 crore. Net interest income grew 24% to ₹11,495 crore. Consolidated assets under management (AUM) reached ₹5.47 lakh crore. The company targets a ₹40 lakh crore AUM by 2036, aiming for a 5% share of India's total credit using AI technology.

articles.headline: High Prices Slash India’s Gold Jewellery Demand by 15% in June Quarter
articles.summary: According to the World Gold Council, India’s gold jewellery demand fell 15% to 89 tonnes in Q2 as prices surged past ₹1.5 lakh per 10g. However, overall demand value rose 50% to ₹1.98 lakh crore. While high volatility discouraged consumers, investment demand for bars and coins grew 59%, and gold ETFs reached 4.2 tonnes, reflecting a shift toward gold as a financial asset.

articles.headline: Cauvery Authority Directs Karnataka to Release Water to Tamil Nadu Amid Shortfall
articles.summary: The Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) upheld an order for Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. Karnataka appealed for a stay, citing a 65% inflow deficit and acute hydrological distress. While farmers in Karnataka protest to protect drinking water, DMK leaders in Tamil Nadu plan demonstrations, claiming the allocation is insufficient.

articles.headline: Swiggy Q1 Loss Narrows to ₹791 Crore as Revenue Grows 37 Percent
articles.summary: Swiggy's net loss for the first quarter narrowed by 34% to ₹791 crore, down from ₹1,197 crore last year. Operating revenue surged 37% to ₹6,812 crore, driven by growth in delivery and quick-commerce segments. While the Instamart arm saw contribution margin improvements, heavy investments continue. The company is focusing on unit economics ahead of its planned IPO.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma Gets Brazil Approval to Launch Generic Semaglutide Diabetes Injections
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has received Brazilian regulatory approval (ANVISA) to manufacture and market generic Semaglutide injections. Used for Type 2 diabetes and weight management, the drug will be launched in partnership with Hypera Pharma in two strengths via pre-filled pens. The Brazilian market for this injectable is estimated at $413 million following key patent expirations.

articles.headline: PM Modi Reviews Energy Security and Sailor Safety Amid West Asia Conflict
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired a Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) meeting to assess the impact of the West Asia conflict on India. He directed officials to ensure stable energy imports and uninterrupted fertilizer supplies for the Rabi season. The committee also focused on establishing support systems for Indian sailors and protecting the diaspora amid maritime tensions.

articles.headline: Parliament Passes Public Examinations Bill to Curb Paper Leaks and Cheating
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill 2026, finalizing the legislation to tighten laws against paper leaks in national competitive exams like NEET. While the government says the bill will bolster the system and include NTA restructuring, the Opposition staged a walkout, demanding a Supreme Court-monitored probe into recent irregularities.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Declines to Ban Pellet Guns for Crowd Control Purposes
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated that pellet guns cannot be banned as long as guidelines permit their use in "exceptional circumstances" for crowd control. A bench led by CJI-designate Sanjiv Khanna emphasized that alleged misuse must be investigated case-by-case. The court also ordered the Delhi government to provide specialized medical treatment for protesters injured during recent demonstrations.

articles.headline: NATO Scrambles Jets After Russian Missile Violates Polish Airspace During Ukraine Strikes
articles.summary: NATO fighter jets were scrambled after a Russian missile entered Polish airspace during a barrage on Ukraine that killed at least eight civilians. The missile landed in Poland's Lublin province, creating a 10-meter crater but causing no injuries. NATO condemned the "reckless act," while Polish authorities noted there was no evidence that Poland was an intentional target.

articles.headline: Parliament Passes Bill Making Insult to National Song a Criminal Offence
articles.summary: Parliament has passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, granting the National Song, 'Vande Mataram', the same legal protection as the National Anthem. Intentional insults to the song are now a punishable criminal offence. While the government claims the bill ensures respectful conduct, the Opposition raised concerns regarding potential misuse.

articles.headline: Delhi High Court to Hear Umar Khalid’s Bail Plea in Riots Case
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court is set to hear an appeal by activist Umar Khalid challenging the denial of bail in the 2020 Delhi riots "larger conspiracy" case. Khalid, arrested in September 2020 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), argues that the prosecution lacks evidence linking him to the violence and that his prolonged incarceration without trial is unjust.

articles.headline: Delhi Jal Board Threatens to Seal Properties of Major Water Bill Defaulters
articles.summary: The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has issued notices to 1,025 commercial property owners with outstanding water dues exceeding ₹25 lakh. Defaulters have until August 15 to clear arrears or face property attachment and sealing. The agency aims to recover ₹5,000 crore in principal dues to fund infrastructure upgrades, while offering a ₹11,000 crore waiver on late-payment surcharges.

articles.headline: Akal Takht Rejects Punjab Government’s Response on Proposed Anti-Sacrilege Law
articles.summary: Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj has rejected the Punjab government's response regarding the proposed anti-sacrilege law, terming it "unsatisfactory." The Takht demanded a fresh draft within two months that incorporates suggestions from Sikh scholars for stricter punishments. Sikh legislators have been directed to halt Assembly discussions until a religious consensus is reached.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Questions Absence of Judicial Member in Election Commissioner Selection Panel
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has questioned the lack of a judicial member in the new panel for appointing the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. While the Union government argued that the Prime Minister's decisions should be trusted, the bench emphasized the need for a "show of fairness." The court reserved judgment on petitions challenging the 2023 Act.

articles.headline: Academicians Condemn Priyanka Gandhi’s ‘Gaumutra’ Remark Against IIT-Madras Director
articles.summary: A group of 215 scholars and university Vice-Chancellors issued an open letter condemning Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s "gaumutra expert" remark directed at the IIT-Madras Director. The academics argued that such labels mock traditional knowledge systems, lack scientific temper, and undermine the dignity of academic leadership, calling for a more reasoned political discourse.

articles.headline: Murali Sreeshankar Clinches Second Consecutive Commonwealth Games Silver in Long Jump
articles.summary: Indian long jumper Murali Sreeshankar secured his second consecutive silver medal at the Commonwealth Games with a best effort of 8.09m–8.15m. Overcoming difficult wind conditions and a previous major knee injury, he finished behind Jamaica's Tajay Gayle. While disappointed at missing the gold, Sreeshankar expressed gratitude and shifted his focus toward winning gold at the upcoming Asian Games.

articles.headline: Veteran Indian Batter Ajinkya Rahane Announces Retirement From International Cricket
articles.summary: Former Indian captain Ajinkya Rahane has announced his retirement from all formats of international cricket. The 38-year-old middle-order mainstay played 85 Tests, scoring 5,077 runs, and famously led India to a historic series win in Australia in 2020-21. While ending his international career, Rahane plans to continue playing domestic and T20 league cricket while mentoring young talent.

articles.headline: Neeraj Chopra Qualifies for Commonwealth Games Javelin Final Amid Windy Conditions
articles.summary: Defending champion Neeraj Chopra qualified for the Commonwealth Games javelin final despite challenging wind conditions, recording a throw between 79.61m and 82.84m. He tops a field that includes fellow Indians Rohit Yadav and Yashvir Singh, as well as Pakistan’s Arshad Nadeem. The highly anticipated final round raises hopes for multiple podium finishes for India in the event.
